newsitem.title: USA: Odds favor Fed rate hike Tuesday -- Comerica Bank.
newsitem.headline: Odds favor Fed rate hike Tuesday -- Comerica Bank.

text.p: Odds favor the Federal Reserve raising interest rates again on Tuesday, according to Comerica Bank.

The "Fed Trigger Index" compiled by Comerica, which forecasts the probability of the Fed raising or lowering interest rates in the near future, indicates that another one-quarter percent rate hike is likely at Tuesday's meeting.

Comerica's Fed Trigger Index shows a 56 percent chance that the Federal Reserve will raise rates one-quarter percent, a 44 percent likelihood that rates would be left unchanged, and a zero percent chance that rates would be lowered. When Comerica economists introduced the index on March 6, the Fed Trigger Index showed only a 32 percent chance of an interest rate increase.
On March 25, just prior to the last meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee, the index correctly predicted the March 25 increase.

"Despite favorable inflation reports over the past two weeks, the Fed appears persuaded that another modest rate hike would be an insurance policy against rising inflation and future financial market distortions," said Comerica economist William Wilson.

Comerica's Fed Trigger Index is a monetary model that bases its probability of interest rate changes on the market's expectations for inflation. The index will be released prior to each scheduled meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee, and other times as warranted.
Comerica Inc is a bank holding company headquartered in Detroit that operates banking subsidiaries in Michigan, California, Texas and Florida.
